text: IMD reports that India received 713.3 mm of rainfall from 1 June through 23 September 2026, against 837.7 mm normal for the same dates (1971–2020); its displayed departure is −14.9%.

period.cutoff_convention: IMD graphic labels dates June 1 through September 23; clock hour is not specified. Times in this record encode calendar dates only.

method_path: IMD all-India graphic middle and bottom panels; (713.3 / 837.7 - 1) × 100 = −14.85%, rounding to −14.9%.
limitations: Rainfall departure is not a measure of water supply or a drought declaration.
The graphic is a mutable, provider-rounded image; exact region boundaries and station methods were not reconstructed.

text: In an outlook issued 31 August 2026, IMD forecast that all-India rainfall during September was most likely below normal, its category for less than 91% of the 1971–2020 September average. It also identified areas where normal or above-normal rain was possible. This is a dated forecast, not a measured September outcome; check for any later IMD issue.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: Valid only for September 2026 and superseded by any later outlook.
A rainfall forecast is not a water-supply or crop-loss forecast.

text: According to a 31 March 2026 Ministry of Jal Shakti release, the Union Cabinet approved Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 on 10 March and operational guidelines were released on 22 March. The ministry reported releasing ₹1,561.53 crore to five named states for FY 2025–26. This does not establish state expenditure or service outcomes.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: A ministry announcement/release is a single source chain and is not independent treasury confirmation.
The five named states are Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Maharashtra; this is not a drought-specific emergency measure.

text: In a 2 April 2026 parliamentary reply, the Ministry of Jal Shakti said states and Union territories reported tap-water connections for about 15.82 crore of 19.36 crore rural households as of 3 March 2026. Connection counts do not establish regular or safe service.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: This is an administrative count reported by states and UTs, not a household functionality survey.
Rounded headline counts should not be treated as exact household counts.

text: In a national survey conducted July–December 2018, 58.2% of rural and 80.7% of urban households reported a drinking-water facility within their premises.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: Household responses in a 2018 survey; not a 2026 service measure or quality test.
The rural and urban frames differ from later JJM administrative reports.

text: In the same 2018 survey, 87.6% of rural and 90.9% of urban households said their principal source supplied sufficient drinking water throughout the year.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: Self-reported year-round sufficiency from the principal source, not independently measured daily service or safe quality.

text: A July–October 2024 survey of villages already recorded as covered by Jal Jeevan Mission found that 86.5% of surveyed households with taps had received water in the preceding seven days and 83.6% reported supply on their scheme schedule. The report estimated 80.2% met its quantity threshold; 76% of tested household water samples passed its microbiological checks.

period.cutoff_convention: Dates are calendar precision; 00:00 encodes date only, not a measured cutoff hour.

limitations: Sampled declared-covered villages, not all rural India; weighted household estimates.
Quantity was estimated using flow at one household per habitation, not each household.
The 76% microbiological sample result is not the share of fully safe or functional households.
The report calculated a separate 76% functionality figure as the minimum of three separately estimated components, not a joint household observation.

text: Karnataka’s 22 September 2026 gazetted order declared 53 additional taluks across 17 districts drought-affected for the 2026 kharif season: 51 severe and two moderate. The order took effect immediately for up to six months unless revoked. It authorizes district authorities to undertake relief under SDRF norms and directs a joint crop-loss survey; it does not establish that aid was delivered or losses measured.

period.cutoff_convention: Order date has calendar precision; 00:00 is a date placeholder, not a signing time.

method_path: Independently counted 53 numbered annex taluks, 51 severe and two moderate, in 17 distinct named districts.
limitations: The order covers listed taluks, not all of Karnataka or India.
It is a declaration and authorization, not proof of relief distribution, crop losses or household water shortage.
The earlier 101- and 23-taluk annexes were independently reviewed for the separate cumulative claim; this 22 September order itself adds 53 taluks.

text: In its 10 September 2026 bulletin, the Central Water Commission reported 130.554 billion cubic metres (BCM) of live storage in 178 monitored reservoirs, 70.66% of their combined 184.762 BCM live capacity. This monitored cohort is not all reservoirs or total usable water.

period.cutoff_convention: Bulletin status date is 10 September 2026; 00:00 is a calendar-date placeholder, not a measurement hour.

limitations: CWC monitored-reservoir cohort only; not all storage, groundwater, household supply or river flow.
Status date is 10 September 2026; the newer 17 September bulletin was listed but its official PDF returned 404 on 24 September.
Capacity fill and departure from ten-year normal use different denominators.

text: CWC reported that its 50 monitored southern-region reservoirs held 30.467 BCM on 10 September 2026, 54.52% of their combined 55.879 BCM live capacity and below their corresponding-week ten-year normal of 40.827 BCM. This CWC region is not the same geography as IMD’s South Peninsula rainfall region.

period.cutoff_convention: Bulletin status date is 10 September 2026; 00:00 is a calendar-date placeholder, not a measurement hour.

limitations: CWC monitored-reservoir cohort only; not all storage, groundwater, household supply or river flow.

text: In IMD’s completed June–September 2002 South Peninsula (10 subdivisions) series, the four printed monthly totals sum to 466.9 mm, 34.8% below the table’s displayed 1971–2020 normal. This is a rainfall comparison, not evidence that 2026 has reached the same severity.

period.cutoff_convention: Completed calendar months June through September; source values are one-decimal monthly totals, not daily cutoffs.

method_path: Sum IMD printed June, July, August and September monthly totals; (466.9 / 716.1 - 1) × 100 = -34.8% at one decimal.
limitations: Completed June–September seasons cannot be ranked against the current 2026 observation ending 23 September.
The South Peninsula footprint has 10 IMD subdivisions; it is not a set of selected current states.
Brief factual extraction only; do not reproduce the IMD historical table, bulk rows or graphics without a rights decision.

text: In the same IMD completed-season series, South Peninsula rainfall in 2009 summed to 681.6 mm, 4.8% below its displayed 1971–2020 normal, while the all-India total was 709.1 mm, 18.4% below its own displayed normal. National and regional rainfall signals differed that year.

period.cutoff_convention: Completed calendar months June through September; source values are one-decimal monthly totals, not daily cutoffs.

method_path: Sum IMD printed June, July, August and September monthly totals, then (actual / displayed 1971–2020 normal - 1) × 100. South Peninsula 681.6 / 716.1 = -4.8% at one decimal; 2009 India 709.1 / 868.5 = -18.4% at one decimal.
limitations: Completed June–September seasons cannot be ranked against the current 2026 observation ending 23 September.
The South Peninsula footprint has 10 IMD subdivisions; it is not a set of selected current states.
Brief factual extraction only; do not reproduce the IMD historical table, bulk rows or graphics without a rights decision.

text: In its 24 September 2026 weather release, IMD reported extreme rain in coastal Andhra Pradesh and very heavy rain in Odisha, Jharkhand, coastal and south-interior Karnataka, and Telangana during the 24 hours ending 08:30 IST that day. This local event report does not establish reservoir or household-service recovery.

period.cutoff_convention: IMD reports weather realised in the 24 hours ending 08:30 IST on 24 September 2026; start is calendar approximation.

limitations: Qualitative local event report; no rainfall totals or catchment benefit inferred.
A 24 September event can coexist with a cumulative rainfall shortfall through 23 September.

text: In an extended-range bulletin issued 17 September 2026, IMD forecast near-normal rainfall for India as a whole in 24–30 September (Week 2); it did not forecast water supply or rainfall through the 2027 monsoon.

period.cutoff_convention: Week 2 forecast dates from IMD 17 September extended-range bulletin; calendar-date precision.

limitations: Forecast validity ends 30 September 2026; recheck current issue and supersede if IMD publishes a newer bulletin.
A national rainfall category does not indicate individual catchment or household water outcomes.

text: NSO’s Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023–24 factsheet reports that food made up 47.04% of average rural monthly per-person expenditure and 39.68% of average urban expenditure, without imputing selected free government-provided items.

period.cutoff_convention: NSO Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023–24 reference year; fieldwork timing follows source methods.

limitations: National rural and urban average expenditure shares, not income or the food shares of low-income households.
Historical budget context only; no 2026 food-price or water-linked impact inferred.

text: AI Author assessment, issued 24 September 2026: some local water systems may remain under pressure through the coming dry season while others replenish before the next southwest monsoon. This is a low-confidence conditional judgment about differing system responses, not a forecast of which district or household will face interruption.

period.cutoff_convention: Editorial scenario horizon through approximately the beginning of the 2027 southwest monsoon; the actual local replenishment date is unknown and 30 June is not a predicted onset.

method_path: Qualitative conditional water-balance reasoning: where verified usable storage is low and inflows fail to offset withdrawals, buffer may shrink; where subsequent catchment rainfall, source levels and delivery recover, concern weakens. No reservoir-level model, location forecast, probability, or numerical shortage estimate.
limitations: Confidence is low in any geographic or calendar outcome; only the conditional physical mechanism is high-confidence.
The 24 September heavy-rain event may alter local conditions, but its catchment or service effect has not been measured.
IMD 23 September rainfall, CWC 10 September storage, and Karnataka administration refer to different dates, boundaries and indicators.
Revise or withdraw if matched reservoir, well and utility records show recovery or a different stress pattern.
This is original AI-authored site analysis, not an official government forecast or a validated statistical model.

text: Three Karnataka kharif 2026 gazetted orders dated 27 August, 17 September and 22 September list 177 distinct drought-affected taluks in total: 161 severe and 16 moderate. This is a count of administrative declarations by 22 September, not a count of people, measured household shortages, crop loss or relief delivered.

period.cutoff_convention: Kharif 2026 declaration assessment references calendar dates; exact crop/weather observation hours are not specified.

method_path: Independent counts of annexure rows: 101 (89 severe/12 moderate) + 23 (21 severe/2 moderate) + 53 (51 severe/2 moderate) = 177 (161 severe/16 moderate). District+taluk pairs normalized and checked for overlap; 176 machine-split unique pairs plus one manually checked Kadur row.
limitations: The 17 September document preamble misstates all 23 as severe; operative order and annexure support 21 severe/2 moderate.
The orders use taluks as administrative units and do not establish household water service, crop damage, aid delivery, or population exposure.
One 17 September annexure row required manual split; no duplicates were found across the three original lists.
22 September order uses the word additional; this count uses all three original annexures and an explicit overlap check.

text: IMD states that June 2026 was India’s sixth-lowest June rainfall since 1901; among the five lower Junes it names, 2014 is the most recent. This is a June-only rainfall comparison, not a rank for the ongoing June–September 2026 season or a measure of water shortage.

period.cutoff_convention: Completed calendar month June 2026; no within-day cutoff is implied.

limitations: The source PDF p. 1 rounds June 2026 to 103 mm; p. 3 prints 102.5 mm.
A completed June rank cannot be assigned to rainfall through 23 September or to household impacts.

text: IMD states that East & Northeast India received 202.6 mm in June 2026, its second-lowest June rainfall since 1901, after June 2009 in that regional series. This describes June only, not the region’s cumulative rainfall through 23 September.

period.cutoff_convention: Completed calendar month June 2026; no within-day cutoff is implied.

limitations: Official regional monthly attribution; the June region and the current cumulative operational graphic should not be treated as a matched historical season series.
Rainfall rank does not establish drought declaration or service harm.

text: At the Department of Consumer Affairs’ monitored Bengaluru centre, the reported retail onion price was ₹57/kg on 23 September 2026 versus ₹23/kg on 23 September 2025, a ₹34/kg (147.8%) increase from the displayed prices. The centre record does not identify the cause or represent all Bengaluru purchases.

period.cutoff_convention: Two discrete same-calendar-date observations; no values between dates are inferred.

method_path: 57 − 23 = 34 INR/kg; (57/23 − 1) × 100 = 147.826%, rounded to 147.8%; source form exact Bengaluru row at both dates, retail unit corroborated by DCA home national row.
limitations: Single monitored centre with undisclosed sample/transaction volume; not a city average or household bill.
The 2025 historical row was returned by the form on 24 September 2026 and may reflect later corrections.
No causal attribution to rainfall, water scarcity, crop damage, trade or other drivers.

text: On 1 August 2026, the Union government said it had approved ₹2,117.85 crore in advance central SDRF shares for six flood-affected states: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra and Odisha. The release does not document transfer of these new advances or aid delivered to households, and this is not Karnataka drought relief.

period.cutoff_convention: Government announcement date; calendar precision only, not a treasury-transfer timestamp.

limitations: Government announcement and approved amount, not verified treasury transfer or beneficiary outcome.
Flood-specific response; does not describe water conditions in every named state or later dates.

text: In a 26 July 2026 release, the Indian Army reported evacuating more than 790 people during flood operations since 23 July in parts of Gujarat and Dadra & Nagar Haveli, and distributing drinking water and essentials. This is an agency-reported operation output, not a national rescue total or proof of long-term recovery.

period.cutoff_convention: Army-reported operation interval from 23 through 26 July; the release does not give a complete independent event ledger.

limitations: Earlier agency count of 355 by 25 July is part of this operation and must not be added.
Ministry-reported operation output, not independently audited or evidence of enduring service restoration.
